## Introduction This vignette guides you through downloading, processing, and analyzing **Orchidaceae (Orchids)** occurrence data in Australia. Data is sourced from the [Atlas of Living Australia (ALA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchid), enriched with weather station metadata, and visualized in multiple ways. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Load Required Packages and Utilities Load all the helper functions using: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} source("vignette-utils.R") ``` ::: You can edit this script at:\ `ecotourism/vignettes/vignette-utils.R` ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Define Global Parameters ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism_name <- "orchids" organism_title <- "Orchids" taxa <- "Orchidaceae" start <- 2014 end <- 2024 email <- "your_email@email.com" ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Step 1: Download and Prepare Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism <- obs_data(taxa, start, end, your_email=email) |> polished_data() ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Step 2: Save Cleaned Dataset ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mysave(organism_name, organism) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Step 3: Attach Nearest Weather Station ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} attach_nearest_station(organism_name) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Step 4: Load and Preview Final Dataset ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} load("../data/orchids.rda") glimpse(orchids) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Data Analysis ### Preview Dataset ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism <- myload(organism_name) organism |> glimpse() ``` ::: ### Occurrence by State ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> my_count(scientificName, obs_state, f=1) |> as_tibble() ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Visualization We'll focus on selected species for visualization: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mss <- c("Acianthus", "Acianthus fornicatus") ``` ::: ### Spatial Distribution Map ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> filter(scientificName %in% mss) |> plot_map1() ``` ::: ### Weekly Trends ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> filter(scientificName %in% mss) |> plot_bar_week() ``` ::: ### Monthly Trends ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> filter(scientificName %in% mss) |> plot_bar_month() ``` ::: ### Yearly Trends ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism |> filter(scientificName %in% mss) |> plot_bar_year() ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Weather Station Mapping ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} organism <- myload(organism_name) organism |> glimpse() ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ### State-wise Weather Matching Summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summarize_state_frequencies(organism_name) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Pattern Analysis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_monthly_occurrences_by_state(organism_name, mss) plot_weekly_occurrences_by_state(organism_name, mss) plot_seasonal_occurrence_polar(organism_name, mss) plot_monthly_occurrence_map(organism_name, mss) plot_monthly_occurrence_map_by_state(organism_name, mss) plot_monthly_distribution_map(organism_name, mss) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Conclusion You’ve now learned how to: - Access and clean orchid occurrence data from ALA - Add weather station proximity information - Analyze trends for specific genera or species This reproducible workflow can support deeper studies into Orchid ecology and conservation through ecotourism data. ##
